findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: There was no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. Another cook with a valid certification was supposed to be present but came late. Inspector was able to verify the certification validity.  Ensure that there is at least one certified food protection manager present at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: An accumulation of ice and frost was observed in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the ice and frost are cleaned out providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Steaks were observed being stored above fish and shrimp in the standing cooler on the far end of the wall right of the cook line. Education was carried out. The food items in the cooler were rearranged to be stored properly. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The internal surfaces of the coffee makers in all the serving areas within the facility were observed soiled. PIC was made aware. PIC instructed employees to clean and sanitized them immediately while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the coffee makers’ are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
There were no certified food protection manager with an active allergen awareness training certificate present and verifiable at the facility during today’s inspection. PIC did have one however, it had expired since 2021. PIC assured inspector that they would get the training done. Ensure that the training is done to be in compliant with the law.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment:
Repeat

A cook staff employee was observed handling fried foods on pass-through with bare hands. The fries and fried shrimp fell from the plate onto the pass-through surface, and the employee picked up the food items and placed them back on the plate with bare hands. PIC was informed of issue, and will re-educate staff. Ensure staff members are both handwashing and donning gloves prior to handling ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. A second follow-up will be conducted on 3/7/25 to ensure proper food handling is being conducted in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed staff member pick cooked broccoli up with bare hands that had fallen from bowl onto prep surface and place back in bowl. Observed staff member touch lobster and potatoes on plate with bare hands and serve plate. Observed staff member pick up garnish (kale) with bare hands and place on plate. Staff member was interrupted and asked to use gloves; staff member discarded garnish and donned gloves to finish the plate. Informed PIC that bare-handing ready-to-eat (RTE) foods is a direct threat to food-borne pathogen transmission. PIC will educate staff on proper food handling procedures and the importance of wearing gloves anytime they are handling RTE foods. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/4/25 to ensure staff are using gloves to handle RTE foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed ice machines to be soiled with pink slime (mold) and debris. Mold is located on baffles and top of internal portion of ice machine. The machines are located behind prep area where bread is prepared. Informed PIC that ice machines need to be emptied and ice should be discarded before cleaning occurs. Mold and debris on the surfaces of the ice machine can contaminate ice, resulting in food-borne pathogen transmission.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed heating element above pass-through table of cook line to be soiled with dust and food debris. Advised PIC that surface needs cleaned in order to prevent cross-contamination with plates of ready-to-eat food placed under warmer.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed tiled wall between stove and ovens along cook-line to be broken (holes in wall). Observed ceiling of dry storage area to be peeling and damaged. Ceiling tiles in dry storage room were peeling directly over an open bin of flour. Informed PIC of damage and emphasized that surfaces should be in good repair so that they do not accumulate dust, debris, or pathogens. Ensure all surfaces of walls, ceilings, and floors are smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Employee observed to have personal cup in kitchen at a food prep area. The cup was removed to a non food area. Ensure that personal drinks are in designated non food areas so that employees have to break from work to drink. This facilitates proper hand washing prior to the return to food service. 
(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Fans in the kitchen have some dust and soil. Fans were taken down and washed. Fans move air through the kitchen, around food and items intended to be maintained clean, such as clean dishes. The violation was corrected immediately on site. Maintain fans clean to sight and touch. 
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
The facility has red sauce and ranch dressing date marked 3/26/24 in the walk in cooler. These items were discarded at time of inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site. The facility was closed for previous 4 days and is just reopening today. Ensure that foods do not extend past the 7 day date marking. Ensure to properly date mark all TCS foods.  The

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The bar hand sink is not sealed to the wall. Seal hand sink to the wall so that the area is easily cleanable. 

6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed personal items in various areas around the building. There was a water cup and a container of trident gum at the main wait station on the shelf next to salt and pepper. There were personal drink cups on the table next to the employee pizza oven and a purse.  Develop a habit of placing personal items separate from items for the public. 

6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.
